quote: Hypothesis 1b: People report greater predicted             Not supported   Consistent
reason: The original study reported a null difference between expected and remembered Thanksgiving enjoyment (p = .105), and the replication authors separately classify directional Hypothesis 1b (predicted > remembered enjoyment, d = 0.04, p = .496) as 'Not supported' under Findings (Table 17.1, p. 70; also 'no support' on pp. 4, 49) while simultaneously labeling it 'Consistent' with the original article (Table 17.1, p. 70; 'no signal consistent' in Table 9b, p. 41; 'consistent with the original results' on pp. 74, 77). Because the p. 67 evaluation ('The replication is not successful with no signal in an inconsistent direction') substitutes the DV2 Happiness item (d = -0.01) rather than Enjoyment (d = 0.04) and conflicts with the 'Consistent' designation for Hypothesis 1b as well as the 'successful' labels given to parallel null DV2 findings on pp. 68-69, while p. 84 ('partially successful in Thanksgiving Day') is a whole-scenario summary across multiple hypotheses, no unambiguous effect-specific replication success or failure verdict is established.
